title: Code-Switching Detection via Language-Selective Dimensions in Speech Foundation Models
gist: Apple researchers propose a lightweight method that detects code-switching (alternating languages within an utterance) directly from speech by finding language-selective hidden-state dimensions in pretrained speech encoders; the Whisper-small encoder reaches a mean F1 of 0.798 across 14 language pairs.

insights.claim: Code-switching, the alternation between languages within an utterance, is common in multilingual speech but underrepresented in pretraining corpora, so increasing coverage requires finding relevant utterances in large speech collections.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Multilingual speech models have a data-coverage weakness; tools that mine such data cheaply improve voice assistants for bilingual users.

insights.claim: The common approach of transcribing speech and detecting language alternation in the text depends on accurate multilingual transcriptions, which the proposed method avoids by detecting code-switching directly from speech.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Skipping transcription lowers the cost and error propagation of corpus curation pipelines.
insights.locator: One way to find such utterances

insights.claim: The method identifies language-selective hidden-state dimensions in pretrained speech encoders using monolingual recordings, aggregates their frame-level activations into a code-switching prediction, and needs only a small code-switching set to tune a decision rule.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A low-supervision detector built on existing encoders is cheap to deploy for on-device and corpus-building uses.
insights.locator: Specifically, we identify language-selective hidden-state dimensions

insights.claim: The Whisper-small encoder achieves a mean F1 of 0.798 across 14 language pairs in CS-FLEURS, versus 0.776 for a CNN and 0.751 for a HuBERT linear baseline trained for monolingual language identification.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The margin over baselines is modest (about 2 F1 points over the CNN), so the value is in simplicity and low cost rather than a large accuracy leap.
insights.locator: With a small CS set used to tune a decision rule

insights.claim: Pretrained speech encoders already encode the information needed to identify code-switching utterances, making them a lightweight tool for building more representative multilingual corpora.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Suggests existing foundation-model representations can be repurposed for data curation without retraining.
